tier1.text: Intermediate filaments help cells resist tension, the forces that pull cells apart. Each filament is made of long protein strands wound together like a rope. Several proteins can form these strands, and the best known is keratin, which strengthens hair, nails and skin. These filaments also hold parts of the cell in place and link neighboring cells together.

sentences.text: Intermediate filaments help cells resist tension, the forces that pull cells apart.

quotes.quote: Unlike the microtubules, which resist compression, intermediate filaments resist tension—the forces that pull apart cells.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Each filament is made of long protein strands wound together like a rope.

quotes.quote: Intermediate filaments are made up of long fibrous subunits of a protein called keratin that are wound together like the threads that compose a rope.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Several proteins can form these strands, and the best known is keratin, which strengthens hair, nails and skin.

quotes.quote: Several fibrous protein types are in the intermediate filaments. You are probably most familiar with keratin, the fibrous protein that strengthens your hair, nails, and the skin's epidermis.
quotes.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: keratin: type of structural protein that gives skin, hair, and nails its hard, water-resistant properties
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: These filaments also hold parts of the cell in place and link neighboring cells together.

quotes.quote: Intermediate filaments help anchor organelles together within a cell and also link cells to other cells by forming special cell-to-cell junctions.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
